title: Diagnosing Constraint Violations knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Diagnosing Constraint Violations”?
options: It guarantees correct output regardless of schema, permissions, or release version.
It is best handled by removing constraints and skipping error checks.

Schema relationships and query joins describe how rows correspond. Use keys to identify rows, foreign keys to enforce references, and normalization to reduce update anomalies; check one-to-many joins for unexpected row multiplication.
It is a frontend styling feature and does not involve database behavior.
questions.answer_key: Schema relationships and query joins describe how rows correspond. Use keys to identify rows, foreign keys to enforce references, and normalization to reduce update anomalies; check one-to-many joins for unexpected row multiplication.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains: Schema relationships and query joins describe how rows correspond. Use keys to identify rows, foreign keys to enforce references, and normalization to reduce update anomalies; check one-to-many joins for unexpected row multiplication.

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies “Diagnosing Constraint Violations” safely?
options: Judge success only by whether the statement returns any rows, without checking expected behavior or edge cases.
Write a read-only diagnostic checklist and identify which output or time range would confirm your hypothesis.
Skip testing, assume every SQL engine behaves identically, and apply the change directly to production.
Concatenate untrusted input into SQL text and grant administrator privileges to every application user.
questions.answer_key: Write a read-only diagnostic checklist and identify which output or time range would confirm your hypothesis.
questions.explanation: Write a read-only diagnostic checklist and identify which output or time range would confirm your hypothesis. This makes the result reviewable and aligns with a controlled learning workflow.

questions.prompt: Before relying on an example for “Diagnosing Constraint Violations”, what should be verified?
options: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
Run a broad production change before checking the current state.
Ignore version notes and infer behavior from an unrelated database engine.
Assume a successful connection means the query and data model are correct.
questions.answer_key: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
questions.explanation: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
